title: How many states the exact DP for LZ77-style parsing with k repeat-offset slots holds, with and without exact pruning
statement: Model as in theorems/lz77-repeat-slots-exact-pruning (literal 9; repeat of slot j with length L >= REPMIN: 3 + j + gamma(L), slot j to the front; new match with distance d <= i and length L >= 2: 2 + gamma(L-1) + gamma(d), d pushed to the front, last slot dropped; slots initially (1, ..., 1); REPMIN >= 2 except in Theorem C). Theorem C (every REPMIN >= 1; delta = 1 if REPMIN = 1, else 0): for every input of length n the forward DP over (position, slot tuple) holds at most max(1, (i-2)^k) states at position i, at most 3 + sum_{j=1}^{n-2} j^k in total, and its prefix-grouped version makes at most S_0 + sum_{i=1}^{n-1} [S_i (1 + k(n-i-1+delta)) + G_i i (n-i-1)] relaxations; on a^n at least prod_{t=1}^{k} (i-2t) states at position i (2k+1 <= i <= n), and for REPMIN = 1, 2 and n >= 1 the relaxation bound holds with equality; hence the worst case is n^(k+1)/(k+1) + O(n^k) states and n^(k+2)/(k+2) + O(n^(k+1)) relaxations for fixed k. Theorem A: with the exact pruning rule G3 (or G3*) and any comparator rule, on a^n (n >= 3) exactly one state, (1, ..., 1), is kept at every position 0..n-1, position n holds n - 2 states, the total is 2n - 2, and (REPMIN = 2) the pruned DP makes n + k(n-1)(n-2)/2 + n(n-1)(n-2)/6 relaxations. Theorems F1 (k <= 4) and F2 (every k) and Corollary W: over unbounded integer alphabets the G3-pruned DP keeps at least (n - C - 2M + 1)^(k+1)/(2^(k+1) M^k) states on explicit strings of every length n >= C + 2M (constants C, M depending on k; under G3* C + REPMIN), so exact pruning keeps Theta(n^(k+1)) states in the worst case, the order of the unpruned DP. Nothing is claimed for fixed alphabets.

bases: Folklore DP over (position, slot contents): Bloom 2015, blog post '01-23-15 - LZA New Optimal Parse' (not peer-reviewed)
provenance.pending_note: The base is the folklore slot-content DP: Bloom's blog posts contain the DP with the repeat-match offsets in the state and the remark that its state space becomes too big once repeat matches are present (2015), and a {Pos,State} parser (2011); neither post counts the states of the DP with repeat offsets, and neither gives a proof. Beyond the sources read, this note proves the state and relaxation bounds (with and without exact pruning). Three sources that might contain them could not be read (missing_sources): the journal version of the dictionary-symbolwise flexible parsing (DSFP) paper and the full text of Langiu's Zip-case paper (the publisher's site refused automated access; the DSFP preprint was read in full and has no repeat-offset state), and the 2010 thesis 'Parsing algorithms for data compression' (University of Pisa; not consultable until 2050). Whether they contain the results could not be checked, so they may be our own result. Nothing read states these state bounds.
